memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, 'When you take a census of the Israelites to count them, each one must pay the Lord a ransom for his life at the time he is counted. Then no plague will come on them when you number them.'" - Exodus 30:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When Israel was counted, each person had to pay a ransom for his life. Being numbered among God's people was not automatic or free. Every individual counted had to be covered by a ransom price. Life belonged to God, and being included required redemption.

The word "ransom" is significant. It means a price paid to release or cover someone. Every person in that census stood there because something had been paid on their behalf. Their inclusion rested on a payment, not on their own merit or family standing.

Jesus used exactly this word about Himself: the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many (Mark 10:45). If your name is counted among God's people today, it is because a ransom was paid — not silver, but the precious blood of Christ (1 Pet 1:18-19). You did not earn your place in the census of God's household. You were bought into it. Let that produce deep gratitude rather than any sense of entitlement.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I recognise that my place among God's people was purchased, not earned?
How should being ransomed shape the way I live today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You gave Your life as a ransom so that I could be counted among God's people. Thank You for such a price paid. Let gratitude, not entitlement, shape my life. Amen.
